description: Navigate the active browser tab to a URL. Reuses the current tab by default (no tab spam). Pass new_tab=true only when you need to keep the current page open. In the current tab the answer is ok:true only when Chrome took the address and the new page is proven loaded within about 25 s (the wait ends half a second before that limit). If the page asks "Leave site?", the default answer is Stay (an armed browser_handle_dialog answers instead) and the reply is error beforeunload-blocked with the tab's actual url: the page may hold unsaved work, so ask the user (browser_ask_user) before you call again with leave_page:true. Other errors, each with sent (was the address sent to Chrome?) and a note on what to do: navigation-in-progress (another navigate is working in this tab, or - with op_id null - an earlier answer to a dialog on the tab is not confirmed yet; wait a moment), dialog-open (a dialog is on screen - answer it with browser_handle_dialog), tab-not-responding (busy page, or a dialog Chrome does not show us), navigation-failed, dialog-unconfirmed, navigation-unconfirmed (no load proven in time; may_complete_later and pending_url say it can still happen - read the tab before sending it again; a download or a 204 answer never loads a page and ends here too), tab-closed (Chrome no longer has the tab), session-changed (another call changed the session's active tab while this one waited; nothing was sent).

eget_vindue.description: Requires new_tab. Opens the page in its own Chrome window, without focus unless you pass fokuser:true. Whether Chrome delivers mouse and keyboard input to a window without focus is unmeasured in desktop Chrome (a measurement on 19 Sept probably tested a background tab, because the tab was moved back into the session's first window; fixed in 1.30.2), so read landed in each input tool's answer. On a machine with more than one display, you can put the window on a screen nobody is looking at and pass fokuser:true - but focus is exclusive: while this window has it, whatever the person types lands in it. Use that only on a machine nobody is typing on.

fokuser.description: With eget_vindue: ASK for the new window to get the operating system's focus. Chrome can refuse it. The reply carries what actually happened - read `fokuseret` and `placeret_som_bedt` rather than assuming this worked. Do not rely on vindue_x to keep a run off the user's screen.

leave_page.description: Answer "Leave site?" with Leave instead of Stay (default: false), so unsaved changes on the current page are lost. Only after the user has agreed (browser_ask_user). An armed browser_handle_dialog on the tab takes precedence over this.

new_tab.description: Open in new tab instead of reusing current (default: false). If the session's only tab is still an empty about:blank placeholder, that tab is used instead of opening another.

vindue_bredde.description: With eget_vindue: window width in points.

vindue_hoejde.description: With eget_vindue: window height in points.

vindue_x.description: With eget_vindue: the window's left edge in global screen points. A NEGATIVE value is a display to the left of the main one - that is how you put it on another screen. No tool lists the displays: use a coordinate you know is on an unused screen, and read `placeret_som_bedt` in the reply.

vindue_y.description: With eget_vindue: the window's top edge in global screen points.

name: browser_navigate
